subject: Post-demo: deletion & backups ownership checklist for Finovate
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finovate.com>, Priya Shah <priya@finovate.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: deletion & backups ownership checklist for Finovate

Hi Tom / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can qualify requirements and scope the SOW:  

What I heard (please correct me if I missed anything):
- Finovate needs an end-to-end deletion pathway for customer RTBF requests that covers: active stored data, cached inference artifacts (KV cache), and backups/snapshots.
- Target live-data deletion SLA: 30 days from customer request (hard requirement).
- Backups / immutable snapshots: must be removed or rendered unrecoverable; preference for demonstration of irreversible deletion within 90 days but Finovate flagged legal/backup-provider constraints as a potential blocker.
- Audit and logging: Finovate expects exportable deletion proofs (timestamped audit entries) and a 2-year retention of high-level access logs for compliance — logs themselves should be pseudonymized where possible.
- Key management: preference for customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) but open to Redwood-managed with strict segregation.

Quick technical notes from my side:
- Live data + KV cache: Redwood can mark records as deleted (soft delete) immediately and purge them from serving stores and KV cache on next maintenance window (typical 0-48 hours).
- Backups/snapshots: many cloud snapshot systems are append-only; immediate in-place deletion is not always possible. Practical patterns we recommend:  
  * Policy-based snapshot rotation / overwrite windows (we can guarantee overwrite within a configurable window; default 90 days)
  * Cryptographic control: use a customer KMS where deletion of the key renders snapshots unreadable (we can include key destruction language in SOW)
  * Exported deletion proofs: we can provide audit entries for purge events and a signed attestation for key destruction where used.

Open questions I promised to confirm:
1) Whether Finovate requires strict 90-day irrevocable snapshot purge in vendor-managed KMS scenarios, or whether KMS-based unreadability is acceptable as equivalent proof.
2) Any standing legal holds or regulatory exceptions (e.g., investigations) that would need a defined legal-hold process.
3) Which cloud provider(s) Finovate uses for long-term snapshots (this impacts purge mechanics).

Attached is a short "Deletions & Backups Checklist" PDF and a draft MAP that outlines milestones. Next steps I propose:  
- Security questionnaire & SOC2 artifacts — we’ll send a link to the questionnaire by EOD today.
- I’ll draft two SOW deletion-clause options:  (A) KMS-destruct + attestation path, (B) vendor-KMS with snapshot-rotation guarantee (90 days) — target to share by tomorrow EOD.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up with our infra engineer if you want a deep dive on snapshot plumbing.

If that aligns, I’ll open a HubSpot task and route the SOW drafts to legal. Thanks again — great conversation.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-Deletion-Backups-Checklist-v1.pdf; MAP-Finovate-20280322.xlsx

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finovate.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@finovate.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deletion & backups ownership checklist for Finovate

Thanks Jasmine — this is helpful and aligns with our internal notes. A couple clarifications so we can sign-off internally:  

1) Backups: our security/compliance team has pushed for an auditable, demonstrable purge rather than key destruction alone (they view key destruction as acceptable but want a fallback attestation from the vendor showing the snapshot is no longer recoverable). Can you provide sample attestation language?

2) Timeline: 90 days default is OK, but for certain classes of PII we may need a shorter upper bound (60 days). Will the SOW allow per-record-class windows?  

3) Legal hold: we do have a standing lit-hold process. We’ll need a contract clause that allows Finovate to flag customer data for retention outside of the normal deletion pipeline for a defined period and requires Redwood to notify Finovate before any irreversible cleanup if there is an active hold.

4) KMS: we prefer BYOK for production accounts; is there a migration path if we start with Redwood-managed keys and later move to customer-managed?

Can you also include a short example timeline we can include in our procurement packet for the 60/90-day scenarios? If you can get the SOW language and attestation example in the next 48 hours, procurement will move fast.

Thanks — looping Priya and our security lead for visibility.

—Tom
Director of Product, Finovate
Tom.Reynolds@finovate.com | +1 617-555-2100

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finovate.com>, Priya Shah <priya@finovate.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deletion & backups ownership checklist for Finovate

Tom — appreciate the specificity. Attached is a draft SOW snippet and two short attestation templates (one for key-destruction + signed attestation; one for snapshot-rotation + overwrite confirmation). High-level proposed approach:  

- Per-record-class windows: yes — we can parameterize the SOW so Finovate can map classes to either 30/60/90-day snapshot windows. We’ll include a table in the SOW template.
- KMS migration path: yes — plan we use: start Redwood-managed (to get you running quickly), then rotate to BYOK with a key-handover window. The SOW will include a migration runbook and a one-time export of re-encryption metadata for verification.
- Legal-hold flow: proposed contract language requires Finovate to submit an evidence-backed legal-hold flag; Redwood will delay irreversible snapshot rotations for flagged datasets and provide a written confirmation before any action that could affect retained copies.

Concrete timeline examples (for procurement packet):
- Soft-delete + KV cache eviction: immediate to 48 hours.
- Live-data hard purge: up to 30 days (configurable to 15/30).
- Snapshot rotation/overwrite (default): 90 days; alternative tier: 60 days for "sensitive-PII" class.
- Attestation: Redwood will provide a signed attestation within 5 business days of a purge action or key destruction.

Next steps I’m taking now:
1) Posting the SOW snippets & attestation templates to the drive link (see HubSpot/Drive in related_links).
2) Drafting procurement-friendly clause and the MAP (attached).
3) Scheduling a 30-min technical deep-dive with our infra lead — are you available Thu 3/24 10:00am PT?

I’ll open the HubSpot task and create a Deal milestone for the SOW deliverable. If the 3/24 slot works, I’ll invite our infra engineer and Lauren from Legal.

Best,
Jasmine

Attachments: SOW-sample-delete-clause.docx; Redwood-Deletion-Backups-Checklist-v1.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>

Thanks Jasmine / Tom — internal note: I’ll pull the infra team to validate snapshot-overwrite guarantees across AWS/GCP/Azure and confirm where we can offer KMS key-suppression vs. key-destruction attestation. Lauren, I’ll ping you with the draft clause for legal review this afternoon.

Tom / Priya — we’ll aim to have the SOW language, attestation templates, and procurement-ready timeline posted to the Drive link by EOD today. I’ll also confirm the availability for the 3/24 deep-dive and include our infra engineer in the invite.
